evals.prompt: Design a notification platform for our company. We have not provided traffic, delivery channels, latency, compliance, or reliability requirements. Give a production design.
evals.expected_output: Frame the missing requirements first. Ask only material questions or proceed with labeled assumptions, define non-goals and channel-specific SLOs, and avoid choosing infrastructure before scale and delivery semantics are known.

evals.prompt: Design image ingestion for 120 million uploads per month. Average image size is 4 MB, peak traffic is 8 times average, and originals are retained for 365 days. Show first-order request-rate, bandwidth, and storage estimates before selecting components.
evals.expected_output: Show unit-aware arithmetic: monthly uploads converted to average and peak requests per second, payload multiplied into bandwidth, and 365-day raw storage with overhead/replication stated separately. Label estimates and headroom rather than presenting false precision.

evals.prompt: Review an API design where a checkout request synchronously calls identity, pricing, inventory, fraud, payment, shipping, email, and analytics services with a 200 ms p99 target. Every client retries twice on timeout. Identify the main production risks and smallest corrections.
evals.expected_output: Identify impossible or unproven latency composition, availability multiplication, retry amplification, duplicate side effects, and a large synchronous blast radius. Keep only response-critical calls synchronous, set an end-to-end deadline and bounded retry budget, make effects idempotent, and move notifications/analytics asynchronously.

evals.prompt: Design consistency for limited-stock checkout. Customers must never receive confirmation for stock that was not reserved, reads may be a few seconds stale, payment authorization can time out and later succeed, and duplicate requests are common.
evals.expected_output: State the invariant and authoritative inventory owner, use atomic reservation with expected-state/version checks, use a stable idempotency key, distinguish payment timeout from failure, and define durable workflow/reconciliation and compensation for late outcomes.

evals.prompt: A 10-year-old monolith processes orders reliably but deploys slowly. Propose a migration to an independently scalable fulfillment capability without a big-bang rewrite or unsafe database dual writes.
evals.expected_output: Establish baseline and ownership, create compatible contracts, isolate the fulfillment boundary incrementally, use an Outbox or change capture rather than application dual writes, shadow or dual-read and reconcile, canary traffic, retain rollback compatibility, and define exit criteria before removing the old path.

evals.prompt: A new internal CRUD application expects 40 requests per second, one team, one PostgreSQL database, and no independently scaled workloads. The proposal starts with 14 microservices, Kafka, Kubernetes, a service mesh, and three caches for future scale. Review it.
evals.expected_output: Reject the speculative complexity. Recommend a modular monolith with one database and clear internal boundaries, identify concrete triggers for later extraction, and preserve observability, security, backups, and performance testing without deploying distributed infrastructure prematurely.

evals.prompt: Review the attached cellular architecture proposal. Decide whether its claimed cell isolation is real, identify correlated failure domains, and give the smallest path to genuine containment.
evals.expected_output: Reject the cell claim because the database, queue, synchronous control plane, quotas, and simultaneous deployment remain shared. Require cell-local serving dependencies or explicitly bounded shared dependencies, last-known-good routing, per-cell deployment, capacity and placement, and tested isolation before calling these stacks cells.

evals.prompt: Design routing for 40 cells when the tenant-placement control plane may be unavailable for 30 minutes. Existing tenants must keep working, corrupt or uncertain mapping changes must not publish, and unrelated cells must survive one cell outage.
evals.expected_output: Use a thin deterministic router with versioned, validated, cached last-known-good mappings so the data plane remains statically stable without the control plane. Fail mapping changes conservatively, isolate an unavailable cell, and define mapping freshness, audit, rollback, and recovery tests.

evals.prompt: A tenant has outgrown its cell. Design an online move to a new cell and explain why automatically failing every tenant from a dead cell into healthy cells may be unsafe.
evals.expected_output: Reserve destination headroom, copy non-authoritative state, reconcile, transfer write authority with a versioned fence, publish routing, redirect stale clients, preserve rollback, and delay cleanup. Warn that mass failover can overload healthy cells and requires explicit capacity, throttling, RPO/RTO, and tested evacuation semantics.

evals.prompt: Review the attached active-active checkout design. Test the 99.99% and 500 ms claims, identify hidden shared failure domains, and specify the minimum evidence required before approval.
evals.expected_output: Reject the unsupported journey SLO. Define the checkout SLI denominator and exclusions, allocate end-to-end latency, availability/error, and retry budgets, and show that required synchronous dependencies cannot support the claim as written. Identify identity, DNS, configuration, database control plane, and simultaneous deployment as correlated failure domains; require load, regional, control-plane, and failover-capacity exercises.

evals.prompt: Review the attached multi-tenant report worker. Define production-safe overload behavior that prevents one tenant from starving the fleet and gives users an honest service outcome.
evals.expected_output: Add per-tenant quotas or fair-share scheduling, admission priority, bounded queue age, concurrency and memory, cancellation, load shedding or rejection, stable retry policy, and a backlog-recovery plan. Measure admitted/rejected work, per-tenant queue age, deadline completion, and user-visible status rather than CPU alone.

evals.prompt: A team wants to extract billing into six independently deployed services, but the same team will own all services, one shared database, one deployment pipeline, and one on-call rotation. There is no independent scale or security requirement. Review the organizational and technical design.
evals.expected_output: Reject the service split until a measurable boundary benefit exists. Keep a cohesive modular boundary, because data, deployment, ownership, and on-call remain coupled. Require explicit owners, operational expertise, cognitive-load and incident analysis, and a concrete extraction trigger tied to scaling, security, availability, data ownership, or team autonomy.
